deferred: Classification proofs for convex bodies, all convex functions, geometric convex functions, and Hausdorff isometries remain cited research results.
Classical and functional Santalo inequalities, Brunn-Minkowski and the ball-summand rolling theorem remain explicit external inputs.

Generalized curvature, floating-body limits, affine surface area inequalities and the nonsmooth extension are not developed locally; 0R15 defines the smooth case and research statements explicitly refer to the source extension.
One-dimensional geometric-function classification, cone-lattice uniqueness, transport interpretation and differential-equation applications are not expanded into separate new branches.
Weighted geometric-function inequalities 0R0N-0R0P are stated on bounded unit sublevel sets containing a neighborhood of zero; degenerate extensions are not claimed proved.
Inverse-power pseudocone inequality 0R0W assumes the reflected perspective set is a compact convex body containing zero in its interior; zero-times-infinity cases are excluded.
Gaussian pseudocone theorem is stated for the unit-nearest-point normalization only; arbitrary-distance extensions and the full weighted Prekopa-Leindler proof remain external.
Introductory slicing/thin-shell progress is contextual and not independently integrated; no fresh general research-status survey beyond the report and specified primary passages.
No old tree, navigation, global audit, synchronization, full-site build, commit or push is modified or run.

entries: One research narrative linking the central order-duality question to three different geometric classes; links are navigation, not prerequisites.
Defines polar constraints and the ambient closed-convex classes with explicit origin and boundedness conventions.
Defines the support encoding of a convex set and its elementary Minkowski arithmetic.
Proves nearest-point separation in finite dimensions without an unproved Hahn-Banach invocation.
Proves the bipolar closure formula including the zero-threshold separation case.
States one external body order-antimorphism classification and retains n>=2.
Defines proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions via closed epigraphs; separates degenerate infinities.
Defines Legendre-Fenchel conjugation, its order reversal and epigraph constraints; involutivity is a consequence link.
Proves biconjugacy through affine minorants, including the vertical separating-hyperplane case and properness.
States the full external affine/scaled order-antimorphism classification and checks why scaling cannot be omitted.
Defines exponential functional volume and its barycenter normalization.
States the centered classical Santalo inequality with ellipsoid equality and linear-volume invariance.
States the exponential Legendre Santalo inequality with finite positive mass and a specified barycenter.
Proves that the quasi-involution axioms induce an involution precisely on the image class.
Proves the symmetric-relation representation and uniqueness on an arbitrary set.
Defines geometric convex functions and explains the fixed-origin restriction.
Constructs and proves functional polarity by reflected epigraph polarity, including zero and infinity conventions.
Computes the two different duals of a convex indicator; one comparison on one input family.
States the external two-class classification with the missing positive scalar restored.
States the external even exponential polarity bound and checks its scale on the Euclidean norm.
Defines the perspective gauge transform and explicitly cites its identification with LA=AL.
Constructs a single homogenized cone and its compact section, retaining closure at coordinate boundaries.
Computes section volume V/(n+1) and the induced J invariance.
Derives the exact n+1-dimensional polar-volume conversion with horizontal factor 2^n.
Proves the even weighted bound by slice polar inclusion and an explicit binomial integral.
Derives the sharp J-self-dual bound from central symmetry and checks the quadratic normalization.
Defines pseudocones and reversed half-space polarity; gives nonemptiness and bipolar reasoning locally, without using 0R0R as a prerequisite.
Proves that the nearest point becomes p/|p|^2 under pseudocone polarity.
Proves the normalized epigraph/conjugate-range criterion in n-1 variables.
Derives the pseudocone functional dual formula and computes its canonical hyperbolic fixed point.
Proves the perspective-reflection correspondence and negative-polar identity; does not assume all images are compact.
States the external Gaussian product bound with the correct standard Gaussian density.
Proves the inverse-power product bound with n*kappa_n/2 normalization and nondegenerate body assumptions.
Defines unit-ball duality, its two image-class conventions, and ball hulls.
States the external ball-summand theorem and its exact signed support formula.
Proves semilinearity of ball duality from the external summand characterization.
States the external classification of not-necessarily-surjective isometries and explains the dual isometry mechanism.
Proves the ball volume-product bound and all translated-ball equality cases from named external inputs.
Proves the fixed-point/constant-width equivalence within ball bodies; the minimum-volume problem is a separate consequence.
States one fixed-volume surface-area conjecture, distinguishing lenses from two-point ball hulls.
States the finite-center intersection contraction conjecture and checks its direction on a constant map.
Defines the smooth c-affine surface area with positive outer-normal curvature convention.
States one external absolute maximum theorem and computes the optimal radius inside the ball family.
States the external c-affine product theorem with translation-invariant equality conditions.
Proves the order-theoretic obstruction to duality on all closed convex sets.
States the precise external Brunn-Minkowski input and its positive-volume equality condition.
One source record preserving report attribution, license and the primary-source locations used for corrections.

source_discrepancies.decision: The displayed formula omits affine input/output terms and a positive multiplier. 0R09 uses 2007 author Theorem 5 instead. The map 2L directly disproves the unrestricted shortened formula.
Use proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions for Legendre self-maps. Constant +/-infinity are mentioned only as paired degeneracies in the all-subsets epigraph setting.
Restore positive multiplier a and two-sided order-reversal hypothesis from JEMS Theorem 4; distinguish involution and arbitrary order anti-isomorphism.
Keep V(f)=integral(1+f)^(-n-1), so |K_f|=V(f)/(n+1); do not identify the two without the factor.
Use direct slice volumes |K_t||L_s| <= kappa_n^2(1-st)^n. This avoids the inconsistent root convention and swapped indices in the printed f,g proof.

Do not use the unrestricted equivalence: lower-dimensional effective domains can have zero exponential integral and unbounded levels. All nondegenerate body arguments state unit-sublevel neighborhood assumptions.
Function domain is R^(n-1), and finite conjugate values lie in [-1,0], not the [0,1] typo in its proof.
Standard n-dimensional Gaussian requires (2*pi)^(-n/2), not (2*pi)^(-n). The perspective Jacobian is t^(-n-1).
Perspective-reflected images can be unbounded or lower-dimensional. 0R0U calls them closed convex sets; 0R0W explicitly imposes compact full-dimensional body assumptions.
With kappa_n the whole unit-ball volume, integral_R^(n-1)(1+|x|^2)^(-n/2) equals n*kappa_n/2. Correct sharp square constant in 0R0W is (n*kappa_n/2)^2.
Brunn-Minkowski RHS is kappa_n^(1/n); the ratio of complementary radii is (1-r)/r. Local proof derives equality through the sum identity without the printed ratio slip.

Printed contraction inequality <= is contradicted by a constant map applied to a half-unit ball. Retain the consistent finite-center Conjecture 6.1.2, and give the direction test in 0R14 rather than import the false variant.
Restore translations of the half-unit ball. Verified against translation covariance and the primary c-affine paper Theorem 5 proof.
